title: Kathleen Kenyon's birth chart
metaDescription: Kathleen Kenyon's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.3° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 15.6° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 14.3° Capricorn: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Venus. A earth sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Sagittarius (21.3°), Venus in Capricorn (4.7°), Mars in Pisces (6.8°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste for the substantial and the lasting, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Pluto is the closest call of the day, an opposition within 0.0°. An opposition is the tradition’s tug of war. Both ends are real, and the work is holding them at once rather than picking a winner. Behind it, Venus conjunction Uranus at 0.3°, and Mars sextile Uranus at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Taurus at 15.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Sagittarius at 21.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aquarius at 29.7° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: earth 5, water 2, air 2, fire 1 across the elements, and cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 3 across the modalities. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 15.6°.
